summary: M.S. Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Developed real-time embedded systems using FreeRTOS, bare-metal C, and UART/I2C/SPI protocols — from PCB design through hardware-in-the-loop debugging with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt + Matplotlib GUI for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment; used GitLab for version control.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Deployed YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson for object detection; sent real-time control commands to STM32 over UART for multi-servo PWM tracking with interrupt-driven override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensor and OLED display over I2C.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal C: timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C display driver.
Programmed GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 peripherals directly; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with PWM and range-gated contact detection via TCA9548A I2C multiplexer and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors.
Resolved 11 hardware integration failures (servo crosstalk, I2C bus conflicts, sensor false positives); achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on physical UR5e via ROS 2 driver; derived DH tables and validated forward kinematic chains for 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B (<2mm repeatability).

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
